title: Reuse exact canonical TypedAxis label tuples
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: After G1-TENSOR-01CD removed the redundant TypedAxis label-index mapping, TypedAxis.labels became the sole canonical label identity/order for relation-block axes. TypedAxis construction still unconditionally materialized a sorted list and then a fresh tuple even when the caller supplied an exact immutable tuple that was already validated in canonical strict order. This duplicated the container and sorting work on the canonical path.
primary_claim: TypedAxis now validates an exact tuple in one ordered pass and retains that same tuple by object identity when it is already strictly canonical. Non-tuple or non-canonical input still falls back to the existing deterministic sort path, and duplicate labels still fail closed. Relation signatures, CSR canonicalization, semiring behavior, Fourfold subject identity, wire serialization and digest semantics are unchanged.
gardener_decision: Reuse the one canonical immutable labels tuple instead of adding a cache, label-index object or second axis representation. Keep the deterministic sort fallback only for inputs that actually require canonicalization. This reduces canonical-path materialization and sorting rather than optimizing for source-line count.
acceptance: an exact already sorted unique tuple of 256 TypedAxis labels is retained by object identity after validation
non-canonical TypedAxis labels are still sorted deterministically
duplicate labels still fail closed without a hash-set duplicate detector
relation-block coordinate construction and point lookup continue to use canonical sorted labels
